_comment: Findings from `npm run audit:identity` that have been investigated and do not need
action. Without this, the audit reports the same ten settled items every run and the
next person re-derives all of them — which is how a guard stops being read.
real-and-correct  the data is right; the check is doing its job by surfacing an
extreme or a legitimate repeat. Nothing to do, ever.
deferred          the finding IS a defect, but fixing it was consciously postponed.
Still counted separately so it cannot quietly become permanent.
Anything not listed here is a NEW finding and is what the exit summary counts.
Removing an entry makes the finding reappear — that is the intended way to reopen one.

steep.why: 4,720 ft over a 1.6 km one-way approach really is a 0.90 average grade. Johannesburg's NE buttress rises straight off the Cascade Pass road. Confirmed by a dedicated audit of all 749 WA dist_km values, and re-confirmed after two incorrect 'corrections' of mine (14.2, then 7.1) were reverted.

Big Four's north face is 4,200 ft tall and the Spindrift Couloir is 4,000 ft of climbing (matching its own length_m of 1219), rising off a 1-mile approach trail. One of the steepest faces in the Cascades.

duplicateRoutes.why: Three rows share the name but carry different grades (V3-4 / V2 / V3) with the same FA (Flying Zebra) — a variation set, not one climb entered three times. The rows' own `corrections` field records the same conclusion.

numericContamination.why: Two 3-metre boulder problems on different blocs sharing a common name. A 3 m height is not a shared measurement, it is what a boulder problem is.
